precepts.text: The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David, of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne.
precepts.point: In Isaiah 7 Ahaz would not ask a sign, so the Lord gave one: a virgin shall conceive and bear a son named Immanuel, and before the child knew to refuse the evil the land of the two kings, Syria and Ephraim, would be forsaken; the sign was the child.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
The promise to David was sworn: “The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne.”

The Lord swore it in truth, and he will not turn from it. The king on David's throne would be the fruit of David's body. That is the same promise as 2 Samuel 7:12, the seed that shall proceed out of David's bowels.

So when the angel said to Joseph, “Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost”, that which is conceived in her is of the prophecy: the fruit of David's body that the Lord swore to set upon his throne. The line runs through Joseph, the son of David.

“And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.” The son is the fruit of David's body, sworn in truth, set on David's throne.

precepts.text: Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness; and let thy saints shout for joy. Job put on righteousness and it clothed him.
precepts.point: If I laughed on them, they believed it not: Job had an austere spirit. I chose out their way: he counseled and directed them. And sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners. Job sat like a king in the army.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

precepts.why:
“I put on righteousness, and it clothed me: my judgment was as a robe and a diadem.” That shows you how Job used to dress. The way he dressed, that is how his righteousness reflected.

“Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness; and let thy saints shout for joy.”

That is why it was written down beside Job 29:14. Sometimes you just scribble in your Bible, and when you look at it again you see why. God wants his priests clothed with righteousness, and Job put on righteousness and it clothed him. His outward robe and diadem matched the righteousness he walked in, and the saints shout for joy when the righteous are clothed that way.

precepts.text: If thy children will keep my covenant and my testimony, their children shall also sit upon thy throne for evermore.
precepts.point: The testimony is the commandments of the Most High. If the children keep his covenant and his testimony, their children shall sit upon the throne for evermore; and it is his testimony, not our own testimony, that is righteous and very faithful and that changes the people.

note.label: Numbers 10: The Silver Trumpets and the Order of the Journeys

precepts.why:
The cloud was taken up “from off the tabernacle of the testimony.” The testimony is the commandments of the Most High.

“If thy children will keep my covenant and my testimony that I shall teach them, their children shall also sit upon thy throne for evermore.” The testimony is what He teaches, and keeping His covenant and His testimony is what puts the children on the throne for evermore.

So the tabernacle the cloud rested on was the tabernacle of His commandments, and Israel took their journeys out of Sinai following the God whose testimony they were to keep.

precepts.text: The Lord has sworn in truth unto David, that of the fruit of his body He would set upon his throne.
precepts.point: The Most High has made a covenant with His chosen and sworn unto David His servant that his seed will be established forever and his throne built up to all generations. Because he was the seed of David, the doctrine of the virgin birth denying that lineage is blasphemy against the Bible, vain lies.

note.label: Psalm 89: The Covenant Made with David

precepts.why:
“I have made a covenant with my chosen, I have sworn unto David my servant, Thy seed will I establish for ever, and build up thy throne to all generations.” Psalm 132 tells what that oath was: “The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne.”

The Lord has sworn in truth unto David, and he will not turn from it, that of the fruit of his body he would set upon his throne. The seed of David, the fruit of his body, sits on the throne.

Christ is that seed. Because he was the seed of David, the doctrine of the virgin birth denying that lineage is blasphemy against the Bible, vain lies. The covenant was sworn to the fruit of David's body, and the Most High's faithfulness to it is established in the very heavens.

precepts.text: Fools because of their transgression and their iniquities are afflicted.
precepts.point: We get afflicted because of our sins, and the Most High calls us fools. Yet these scriptures were written for our learning so that through patience we might have hope.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why:
“Lord, remember David, and all his afflictions”. The affliction refers to David’s sins. If you know David’s history, he did foolish things, got one of his best men killed and took his wife. “Fools because of their transgression, and because of their iniquities, are afflicted.”

We get afflicted because of our sins, and the Most High calls us fools. Yet these scriptures were written for our learning, so that through patience we might have hope.

precepts.text: Exalt the Most High and worship at his footstool, for he is holy.
precepts.point: Holy means severed. We were severed from other people, given a set of laws contrary to all nations. Once we mingle with the other nations we become unholy.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why: “We will go into his tabernacles: we will worship at his footstool.” “Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship at his footstool; for he is holy.” We come into the house of the Most High to learn his laws, to be holy, to be separate, because he is holy.

precepts.text: You shall be holy unto me, for I have severed you from other people that you should be mine.
precepts.point: Holy means severed. We were severed from other people, given a set of laws contrary to all nations. Once we mingle with the other nations we become unholy.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why: “And ye shall be holy unto me: for I the Lord am holy, and have severed you from other people, that ye should be mine.” Holy means severed. We were severed from other people and given a set of laws contrary to all nations. That is what we come into his tabernacles to learn: to be holy, to be separate. Once we mingle with the other nations we become unholy.

precepts.text: Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God; keep other doctrines away, for the sacrifice of fools is evil.
precepts.point: Holy means severed. We were severed from other people, given a set of laws contrary to all nations. Once we mingle with the other nations we become unholy.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why: “Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.” When we go into his tabernacles to worship at his footstool, we keep our foot: keep other doctrines away, for the sacrifice of fools is evil. We come to hear his laws and be holy.

precepts.text: The woman says the Messiah which is called Christ is coming; Jesus says, I that speak unto thee am he.
precepts.point: Anointed means the smearing of oil, but this goes deeper, into Christ. David was anointed too, but this points to the Messiah who is called Christ.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why: “For thy servant David’s sake turn not away the face of thine anointed.” Anointed means the smearing of oil, but this goes deeper, into Christ. “The woman saith unto him, I know that Messias cometh, which is called Christ: when he is come, he will tell us all things. Jesus saith unto her, I that speak unto thee am he.” David was anointed too, but the anointed here points to the Messiah who is called Christ.

precepts.text: God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power, for God was with him.
precepts.point: Anointed means the smearing of oil, but this goes deeper, into Christ. David was anointed too, but this points to the Messiah who is called Christ.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why: “How God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power: who went about doing good, and healing all that were oppressed of the devil; for God was with him.” God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power. That is the anointed whose face is not to be turned away for David’s sake: anointing is the smearing of oil, but it goes deeper, into Christ.

precepts.text: I will set up thy seed and establish his kingdom; he shall build a house and his throne shall be established forever.
precepts.point: Solomon was set up after David and built the house, but the throne established forever refers to Christ. Solomon committed much iniquity and was not chastened with the rod of men; this points to something deeper in Christ.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why:
“The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne.” Here is the oath: “I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom. He shall build an house for my name, and I will stablish the throne of his kingdom for ever. I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men”.

Solomon was set up after David and built the house, but the throne established for ever refers to Christ. Solomon committed much iniquity and was not chastened with the rod of men, so this points to something deeper in Christ. David’s seed will sit on the throne for evermore, as it has been prophesied.

precepts.text: Awake, put on thy strength O Zion, put on thy beautiful garments O Jerusalem the holy city.
precepts.point: The Most High has chosen Zion for his habitation. Zion is called the city of David, but Zion also refers to a people, the Israelites.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why: “For the Lord hath chosen Zion; he hath desired it for his habitation.” Zion is called the city of David, but Zion also refers to a people, the Israelites: “Awake, awake; put on thy strength, O Zion; put on thy beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city: for henceforth there shall no more come into thee the uncircumcised and the unclean.” A city does not awake and put on strength; a people does.

precepts.text: You shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and I am the Most High your God and none else.
precepts.point: His rulership, his throne, will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel forever. He is the Most High our God and none else, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why: “This is my rest for ever: here will I dwell; for I have desired it.” Here he will dwell in the midst of Israel: “And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and none else: and my people shall never be ashamed.” He is the Most High our God and none else, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

precepts.text: The place of my throne where I dwell in the midst of the children of Israel forever.
precepts.point: His rulership, his throne, will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel forever. He is the Most High our God and none else, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why: “Son of man, the place of my throne, and the place of the soles of my feet, where I will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel for ever”. This is the rest for ever where he will dwell. His rulership, his throne, will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel for ever.

precepts.text: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
precepts.point: His rulership, his throne, will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel forever. He is the Most High our God and none else, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why: “I will abundantly bless her provision: I will satisfy her poor with bread.” Her poor are the poor in spirit, the Israelites: “Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.” He satisfies them with bread and the kingdom is theirs.

precepts.text: Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life and enter through the gates into the city.
precepts.point: Righteousness goes into the commandments. That is how we get salvation, the kingdom of heaven, eternal life.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why: “I will also clothe her priests with salvation”. The priest will teach our lost people how to get salvation, and salvation comes by doing the righteousness of this book, keeping the laws of the Most High: “Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.” That is how we get salvation, the kingdom of heaven, eternal life.

precepts.text: It shall be our righteousness if we observe to do all these commandments.
precepts.point: Righteousness goes into the commandments. That is how we get salvation, the kingdom of heaven, eternal life.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why: “And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.” Righteousness goes into the commandments. The priests clothed with salvation teach our lost people that salvation comes by doing the righteousness of this book, and this is what that righteousness is: observing to do all these commandments.

precepts.text: He exalts the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints, even the children of Israel near unto him.
precepts.point: The lamp ordained for the anointed is Christ, the light that came into this world of darkness. The commandment is a lamp to correct us, a reproof and instruction in the way of life to get eternal life.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why: “There will I make the horn of David to bud”, meaning become a leader. “He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel, a people near unto him. Praise ye the Lord.” The horn refers to Christ, our leader, raised up among the saints, the children of Israel, a people near unto him.

precepts.text: Blessed be the Most High of Israel, for he has raised up a horn of salvation in the house of his servant David.
precepts.point: The lamp ordained for the anointed is Christ, the light that came into this world of darkness. The commandment is a lamp to correct us, a reproof and instruction in the way of life to get eternal life.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why: “Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David”. The horn of David made to bud is Christ, the horn of salvation raised up in the house of his servant David, our leader among the children of Israel.

precepts.text: The commandment is a lamp and the law is light, and reproofs of instruction are the way of life.
precepts.point: The lamp ordained for the anointed is Christ, the light that came into this world of darkness. The commandment is a lamp to correct us, a reproof and instruction in the way of life to get eternal life.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why: “I have ordained a lamp for mine anointed.” The lamp ordained for the anointed is Christ, the light that came into this world of darkness. And “the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life”. The commandment is a lamp to correct us, a reproof and instruction in the way of life, to get eternal life.

precepts.text: God will not cast away a perfect man; they that hate thee shall be clothed with shame and the dwelling place of the wicked come to nought.
precepts.point: The evildoers hate the light and love darkness. But upon Christ his crown, his rulership, will flourish forever, because he has budded as a leader and his second coming will flourish forevermore.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why:
“His enemies will I clothe with shame: but upon himself shall his crown flourish.” “Behold, God will not cast away a perfect man, neither will he help the evil doers: Till he fill thy mouth with laughing, and thy lips with rejoicing. They that hate thee shall be clothed with shame; and the dwelling place of the wicked shall come to nought.”

The enemies clothed with shame are not only the nations but the wickedness of our own people, the evildoers, who will be clothed in shame when the day of judgment comes. The evildoers hate the light and love darkness. But upon Christ his crown, his rulership, will flourish for ever, because he has budded as a leader and his second coming will flourish for evermore.

precepts.text: Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness; and let thy saints shout for joy.
precepts.point: The garment is twofold. The change of raiment is Israel becoming righteous: keeping the commandments, putting the Most High first, and dealing rightly with him and with our own people.

note.label: Zechariah 3: The Filthy Garments Taken Away

precepts.why:
The garment is twofold. Joshua's filthy garments are taken away and he is clothed with change of raiment, and that change of raiment is Israel becoming righteous. “Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness; and let thy saints shout for joy.”

The priests clothed with righteousness is the change of raiment: keeping the commandments, putting the Most High first, and dealing rightly with him and with our own people. When our iniquity passes from us, that is the garment we are clothed with.

precepts.text: Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness; and let thy saints shout for joy.
precepts.point: The garment is not cloth. It is righteousness, which is the keeping of the laws of the Most High.

note.label: Matthew 22: The Marriage of the King's Son and the Great Commandment

precepts.why:
The king found a man “which had not on a wedding garment”, and when asked how he came in without one, “he was speechless.” He was bound hand and foot and cast into outer darkness, “there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth. For many are called, but few are chosen.”

The garment is not cloth. David shows what it is: “Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness; and let thy saints shout for joy.” Righteousness is the clothing, and righteousness is the keeping of the laws of the Most High.

So the man without the wedding garment is one who came to the marriage without righteousness, without keeping the laws. That is why he had no answer for the king, and why many are called but few are chosen.

precepts.text: The Most High sware in truth unto David, of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne; Christ the son of David is that king.
precepts.point: David is dead and buried and his sepulchre is still with us, so he was speaking as a prophet, not of himself. Knowing the Most High had sworn that of the fruit of his loins, the seed and lineage from his body, a king would be raised to sit on his throne, David foresaw the resurrection of Christ.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
This is the oath Peter is talking about: “The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne.” The fruit of his body, the fruit of his loins, is the seed and lineage that came from David's own body.

David is dead and buried and his sepulchre is still with us, so he was not speaking of himself; he was speaking as a prophet. Knowing the Most High had sworn that a king from his seed would sit on his throne, David saw before and spoke of the resurrection of Christ. Christ the son of David is that king.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Breakdown Of Revelation 16

precepts.why: “The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne.” The fruit of David’s body is his sperm: of the seed that comes from your body I will set upon thy throne. So don’t ever think there was such a thing as an immaculate conception; so many precepts in the Bible go against it.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Breakdown Of Revelation 16

precepts.why: “There will I make the horn of David to bud”: the one that comes from the fruit of David’s loins. Who is that? Christ. He is the horn, the leader.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Breakdown Of Revelation 16

precepts.why: Keep your garments: “Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness; and let thy saints shout for joy.” The men and women who left this truth ran out naked, with no garments. In all that confusion nobody came to leadership; if it is a personal problem, the solution is Matthew 18. If there is a problem you apply the scriptures; you don’t run a social media video campaign. That is agent provocateur stuff.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 19 Supper, War & Marriage

precepts.why: I want to talk about righteousness for a second; it goes with us making ourselves ready. “Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness; and let thy saints shout for joy.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

precepts.why:
Your testimony is garbage; this is the testimony God is looking for. “The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne.” Meaning of the sperm that comes from you, I will come and sit on your throne.

“If thy children will keep my covenant and my testimony that I shall teach them,” See what it says about us: if we shall keep the testimony that God teaches us. Not your testimony. The second you get angry you are out the door, and tomorrow you might be a Muslim or a Seventh-day Adventist. God wants to hear the testimony he taught us concerning his Son, and that testimony is more important than anybody in this room.

That verse proves there is no such thing as immaculate conception. For your mothers, fathers, sisters and brothers following an immaculate conception doctrine, that is not the testimony God is looking for. “their children shall also sit upon thy throne for evermore.” The only way we are going to sit on thrones, brothers, is we have to follow the testimony God gave about Christ, that he would come through the seed of David. If you have any other thing in your head, this ain't for you: go on back to Creflo, TD Jakes, Juanita Bynum, Joel Osteen, Billy Graham, Benny Hinn. You don't believe the testimony God gave of his Son, that he would come through the fruit of his loins.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 13 Jesus came to Kenya, A study of his image

precepts.why:
“If thy children will keep my covenant and my testimony”: not your testimony, his testimony. “That I shall teach them”: and he teaches us from the Bible. “Their children shall also sit upon thy throne for evermore”: that is the only way our people are going to rule on this earth.

Verse 11 tells you what the testimony is. “The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne.” What is the fruit of his body? Sperm. Christ came from the seed of David. That is the testimony God wants to hear: that the Messiah comes from the seed of David. That immaculate conception you’re running around with is garbage. We have to believe his covenant and the testimony regarding his son.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 12 Red Dragon, Red Herring

precepts.why: What is the word of their testimony? “Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne”: the fruit of David’s body is Christ, who came from the loins of David. “If thy children will keep my covenant and my testimony that I shall teach them”: we are only going to overcome with God’s testimony that he teaches us about his son. “Their children shall also sit upon thy throne for evermore”: talking about the kingdom of heaven.
